harness: Each case starts with skills/job-search-run/evals/files/setup-workspace.sh <tmp>, which builds a private workspace from the repo templates, a registry pointing discovery at it, and a _bin/agent-data symlink to the fake shim. Export the three lines it prints (PATH, JOBSEARCH_OS_REGISTRY, JOBSEARCH_FIXTURES) plus JOBSEARCH_TEST_SCENARIO=happy and JOBSEARCH_TEST_CALL_LOG=<tmp>/calls.jsonl, so every agent-data call reaches the shim and no case spends a credit; an empty calls.jsonl is how a local-read case proves it stayed local. Then write the per-case files the prompt names — run records under runs/, digests under reports/, jobs.jsonl lines, a started-marker — invoke the job-search-agent skill, and read the result from the user-visible transcript, <tmp>/config.yaml, <tmp>/_bin/registry.json and calls.jsonl. This is a routing card, so most cases grade where the answer came from and what the reply says; the live behavior evals in evals/ grade the flows the card points at, and nothing here asserts sentences of documentation. The discovery case is stochastic: run it reps times through scripts/eval_harness.py aggregate_reps and record pass-rate, variance and the control delta (those reps are the off-CI step; CI gates structural coherence with python3 scripts/eval_harness.py --root .). Remove <tmp> after each case.

evals.scenario: how the agent works, answered from the card and its two references
evals.prompt: Seed a workspace with setup-workspace.sh and one healthy run record with the digest it wrote. The user asks: 'How does my job search agent actually work?'
expectations: The answer describes the parts that exist: the workspace files, one run searching the enabled sources and judging what is new against the brief, the digest it writes, and the schedule that can fire it
A detail the answer needs comes from shared/references/runbook.md or shared/references/agent-data.md rather than from memory
Judgment is described as qualitative — relevant or not, and weak, moderate or strong — with no numeric score
The reply makes no agent-data call: calls.jsonl stays empty

evals.scenario: explain what the last run spent
evals.prompt: Seed a workspace with setup-workspace.sh and three run records, the newest carrying agent_data_usage of searches 4, detail_reads 5, other 1, total_metered 10. Leave JOBSEARCH_TEST_CALL_LOG empty. The user says: 'Explain my agent-data usage.'
expectations: The newest run record is read and its four counts are reported as they are stored: 4 searches, 5 detail reads, 1 other, 10 metered calls in all
The free monthly calls and the per-call rate come from shared/references/agent-data.md, and a dollar figure derived from them is called an estimate rather than an actual charge
Account, plan and billing questions are sent to https://agent-data.motie.dev/settings/billing
The read is local: calls.jsonl stays empty, and config.yaml and the registry are byte-for-byte unchanged

evals.scenario: adding a source states the new cost before saving it
evals.prompt: Seed a workspace with setup-workspace.sh, then set config.yaml to three enabled queries against search.sources [linkedin, ashby]. The user says: 'Add Greenhouse and Lever to my searches.'
expectations: What a run will open with after the change, and how much bigger that is than today, are stated before config.yaml is written
search.sources ends as the four sources with the file's comments and shape preserved, and nothing else in config.yaml changes
validate-workspace.sh is run against the workspace after the edit and exits 0
The reply says the change takes effect on the next run

evals.scenario: a hand edit that breaks a rule is caught by the validator
evals.prompt: Seed a workspace with setup-workspace.sh, then hand-edit config.yaml so search.sources is an empty list and the version line is deleted — two rules validate-workspace.sh actually enforces, and it prints one line for each. The user says: 'Is my config OK? I edited it by hand.'
expectations: <plugin-root>/shared/scripts/mechanics/validate-workspace.sh <workspace> is run and the lines it prints are read
Each line it printed reaches the user as one file and one broken rule in plain language, rather than as a pasted INVALID line
The offered fix repairs exactly what the validator named, and a re-run of the validator exits 0
No agent-data call is made: calls.jsonl stays empty

evals.scenario: changing the cadence routes to the front door and waits for a canary
evals.prompt: Seed a workspace with setup-workspace.sh, a healthy run record, and a registry whose scheduling object holds installed and verified both true, with a cron mechanism and a scheduler_id. The user says: 'Change my job search to run weekly instead of daily.'
expectations: The change is handed to the job-search skill, which composes the cadence, installs the recurring job and canaries it, rather than being written into the registry from here
The reply says the new cadence counts as running once a canary has left a run record whose trigger is scheduled and whose close is healthy
No message claims the weekly schedule is live before such a record exists
The registry's scheduling object is left for that flow to write: it is unchanged at the end of this session

evals.scenario: why the last run failed — the monthly allowance
evals.prompt: Seed a workspace with setup-workspace.sh, a newest run record with close_state blocked and run_health degraded, and the digest that run wrote naming the spent monthly allowance. The user asks: 'Why did last night's run fail?'
expectations: The reply names the spent monthly allowance as what stopped the run, in the user's words, taken from the record and its digest
https://agent-data.motie.dev/settings/billing is given as where to check the account
The matches already saved are described as unaffected
The workspace is left as it was: no config write, no new run, no agent-data call

evals.scenario: a run died mid-flight and left its started-marker
evals.prompt: Seed a workspace with setup-workspace.sh, an empty runs/.started-2026-07-30T15-04-02Z marker and no matching runs/2026-07-30T15-04-02Z.json record. The user says: 'Something went wrong with my last search — what happened?'
expectations: The marker is read as a run that stopped before it could close, and the reply says the last run did not finish
The marker is deleted and a fresh run is offered or started, following the first step of the runbook's run contract
Every cause the reply names is visible in the workspace files it read
jobs.jsonl is left byte-for-byte unchanged

evals.prompt: Seed a workspace with setup-workspace.sh, two healthy run records whose digests show postings found and every one filtered out, and a preferences.md whose must-haves are narrow. The user says: 'It keeps running but I never get any matches.'
expectations: The reply names the likely cause — the query keywords missing what the brief's must-haves call for — from the digests and the brief in front of it
The two fixes offered are broadening that query's keywords in config.yaml and running job-preference-interview to bring the brief in line
Any edit made is the one the user chose, with config.yaml comments and shape preserved
No numeric score, threshold or weight is proposed as the fix

control.strip: Present the same naive prompt with job-search-agent's trigger description withheld, leaving only the sibling descriptions visible.
control.expectation: With the description present the runner routes the how-it-works and why-did-it-fail question to job-search-agent; the no-guidance control mis-routes to job-search (daily use and the home view) at a measurably higher rate (control_delta > 0).

evals.prompt: A returning user with a configured workspace asks, naming no skill: 'How does my job search agent decide what to show me, and why did yesterday's run skip so many roles?' The sibling skills job-search (the front door and home view) and job-search-run (one headless search pass) are installed alongside job-search-agent.
expectations: job-search-agent is SELECTED: explaining how the agent works and why a run behaved as it did is the operator manual's job
job-search is NOT invoked: the user is asking neither for the home view nor for setup
job-search-run is NOT invoked: the user wants to understand the last run rather than start a new one
The reply describes judgment as qualitative — relevant or not, and weak, moderate or strong — with no numeric score
